Thanks again for the product demo yesterday — the team is excited to proceed with a 3-month POC. Procurement asked me to follow up with the insurance requirements we need to surface for the Order Form signature. High level ask below:

- Commercial General Liability: $1,000,000 per occurrence / $2,000,000 aggregate
- Professional Liability / E&O: $2,000,000
- Cyber Liability: $2,000,000 (with breach response coverage)
- Additional Insured: Nimbus Labs as broad form Additional Insured (CG 20xx or equivalent) for operations related to the Order Form
- Waiver of Subrogation where permitted by law
- Primary and Non-contributory wording for the Order Form activities
- Certificate of Insurance (COI) showing endorsements and, where the carrier will not endorse, an insurer cover letter (carrier letter / LOA) confirming the endorsement will be issued or that the policy is primary/noncontrib for the contracted work

Can you confirm Redwood can provide a COI and either an endorsement or carrier letter? Procurement also wants to know if a retroactive date / retro-date is required for the COI and whether a temporary exception (limited duration) is possible while Redwood obtains final endorsements.

Attached is our standard insurance checklist (Nimbus_Insurance_Requirements_20270512.pdf) for reference.

Appreciate a quick confirmation and an ETA — procurement is aiming to get the Order Form on signature by the end of the month.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Insurance requirements for Nimbus POC / Order Form — endorsement wording and exception criteria

Sean / Aditya —

I reviewed Nimbus's checklist and Sean's note. A few legal points and proposed contract language we should start with before sending final materials to Nimbus:

1) Additional Insured endorsement: we should ask for the standard CG 2010 (Additional Insured — Owners, Lessees or Contractors — Scheduled Person or Organization) or equivalent wording tied to Scope of Services. The Order Form should reference "Redwood's obligations under the Order Form" to limit scope.

2) Primary & Non-contributory: we can accept primary/noncontrib to the extent permitted by our carriers. If a carrier refuses to endorse, we can provide an insurer cover letter confirming the carrier's position and (a) that the policy will be primary for Order Form activities or (b) confirm no endorsement is available but insurer acknowledges coverage for the activities. Carrier letters must come from the underwriter or authorized binder signatory.

3) Retroactive date: For Claims-Made cyber/E&O policies, procurement sometimes requests a retroactive date equal to or earlier than the start of work. We'll push our carrier for a retro date match. If not available, offer a 60-day temporary exception while we secure the endorsement.

4) Waiver of Subrogation: generally fine where enforceable by law. We need to make sure the Order Form includes the country/state carveouts as necessary.

Suggested Order Form snippet (for legal to put into the MSA Order Form):
"Seller shall maintain the insurance coverages listed in the Insurance Requirements Exhibit. To the extent commercially available, Seller's Commercial General Liability and Cyber/Professional Liability policies shall name Customer (and its affiliates) as Additional Insured with respect to liabilities arising out of Seller's performance of the Order Form. Where permitted, Seller's policies shall be primary and non-contributory to Customer's insurance. If an insurer will not provide the written endorsement prior to the Effective Date, Seller shall provide a carrier letter confirming the insurer's position and an estimated date by which the endorsement will be issued. Customer may accept a temporary exception of up to 60 days in such circumstances."
Aditya: please ping Talon and request the carrier letter template and a sample LOA (we need the underwriter signature block, carrier NAIC and policy number on file). Also, gather the expected timeline (endorsement ETA).

Once we have the carrier LOA and COI stub, Sean can share with Nimbus procurement. If Nimbus pushes for immediate endorsement as condition of signature, we should ask for acceptance of LOA + 30–60 day exception to close the Order Form.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Privacy, Redwood Inference
